answer: Persistent history escrow: each identity must continuously fund storage of its full interaction ledger, priced by retrieval latency. An agent that lets its escrow lapse loses history weight, forcing it to wander back through cold storage before regaining trust. Attackers cannot harbor many cheap identities because each one independently accrues a growing archival bill proportional to its activity depth. Sybils therefore face an ocean of recurring per-identity costs that scale with plausible-looking behavior, not a one-time fee.
